QF.id: XIII Trading, Clearing, Settlement and Risk Management_42

question.text: In equity derivatives, what are the inclusion (entry) criteria for a stock to be eligible for the futures and options segment?

answer.text: The stock must be in the top 500 by average daily market capitalization and average daily traded value, have a median quarter-sigma order size (MQSOS) of at least Rs 75 lakhs, a market-wide position limit (MWPL) of at least Rs 1,500 crore and an average daily delivery value of at least Rs 35 crore in the cash market over the previous six months
Any stock listed on the exchange for more than 6 months is automatically eligible for F&O trading
Only Nifty 50 constituent stocks are eligible for individual stock futures and options
Stock eligibility is determined solely by market capitalization — top 500 stocks by market cap qualify automatically

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook entry criteria for stock derivatives are: (i) top 500 by average daily market capitalization AND average daily traded value, (ii) MQSOS of at least Rs 75 lakhs (a threshold, not a ranking), (iii) MWPL of at least Rs 1,500 crore and (iv) average daily delivery value of at least Rs 35 crore over the previous six months. All four conditions must be met for initial inclusion. The Trap: Eligibility is not automatic with listing age, Nifty 50 membership or market cap alone. Note also that a minimum 75% trading-days requirement is part of the product success / exit-norm framework, not the initial inclusion criteria, and MQSOS is a hard threshold rather than a ranking input. Note: Once included, stocks must continue to meet ongoing criteria; failure to do so can lead to exit from the F&O segment under prescribed product-success / exit norms.
